tldr: Costed validation can make the average of an adaptive experiment look much more informative than its realized allocation. In the saturated binary-pair model, an exact singleton-entry criterion locates the cell-interiority boundary at which paired validation alone is optimal. Above that boundary, a truncated analytic coin factory makes inverse-expected-information regret exponentially small, while its realized allocation retains a positive precision loss. The minimum expected loss for the realized information criterion instead has order \(n^{-1}\). A pilot-compensated plug-in design attains that order and its pooled pair-mean estimator has oracle first-order variance and uniformly studentized \(90\%\) intervals. The sharp expected-information decay remains a separate open question.
gap: The existing pair-validation proposal leaves the exact support boundary and a matching high-interiority information-regret converse unresolved. Its \(O(n^{-1})\) high-interiority upper bound concerns an inverse taken after averaging information. Published planned-missing and random-normalization results do not characterize the separation between that criterion and the expected inverse of the selected information in this experiment.
fill: The exact support certificate, exponential expected-information construction, and matched \(n^{-1}\) realized-information frontier determine which criterion can support an efficiency statement. An observable pooled estimator supplies the first-order inference interpretation.
